candidates.notes: LICENCE FLAG, and the main finding of this search: Sketchfab no longer has any game-ready car under a CC0 label. The search API with license=cc0 returns only museum and cultural-heritage scans. I ran about 80 queries (car, sports car, race car, supercar, gt3, hatchback, le mans, rally, formula, open wheel, vehicle and more) with paging. The only car-like CC0 item was a 1900s wooden toy scan from the Cleveland Museum of Art (rejected as toy style). The /v3/models endpoint ignores the license=cc0 parameter and returns CC-BY items, so do not trust it. User uploads that were CC0 now carry the 'Free Standard' label: this author's whole public-domain series and Quaternius's Pirate Kit both show it. Free Standard is not on the accepted list, so the owner must decide. The case for these models is that the author's CC0 dedication is written in every description, and a CC0 dedication cannot be withdrawn. MODEL: an original concept design, not a replica, made in Blender in July 2023, with a making-of playlist linked. It is not tagged as AI. Note that the same author has two separate models tagged createdwithai (ConceptCar 049 and 050), which I rejected. This is the most believable modern GT coupe shape in the set: long hood, low roof, large multi-spoke rims. Its proportions loosely recall a modern British GT but it does not copy a specific car. Semi-realistic look with clean materials (pbrType none, 6 textures, 33 materials), so it needs a three.js PBR car-paint pass. 406k triangles, which is over the 200k target, so it needs decimation. It probably has an interior. The previews show distinct wheels and there are 6 animations, but whether the wheels are separate objects is unconfirmed until download. Scale unknown.

candidates.notes: LIKELY REJECT on the resemblance rule. In the screenshot it closely resembles the Tesla Roadster (2nd gen, 2017 prototype): no grille, slim headlight slits, glass targa roof, same proportions. Technically it is the best web-ready asset found: optimised glTF/GLB (also KTX2+Draco), 213,347 triangles (counted from the glTF JSON), meter scale (~4.5 m long), separate named wheels/rims/brake discs per corner, opening doors/hood with correct pivots, a full interior, KHR clearcoat/transmission/iridescence, and 3 material variants. Licence caveat on the upstream: Unity Fan's Sketchfab concept cars (001-040 etc.) are titled 'public domain (CC0)', but the Sketchfab licence field now says 'Free Standard'. That Sketchfab/Fab Standard licence is revocable, single-seat, and forbids making content extractable by end users. Some of his later ones ('Ai based ConceptCar 049/050') are AI-based. The Khronos derivative is clean CC-BY 4.0 because it was made while the original was CC0. Licence findings for the other sources searched, all rejected: (1) Fab.com 'Standard'/free assets: the EULA says 'you must restrict end users from extracting or otherwise using Content outside of the Project', which raw glTF in three.js does not satisfy, and it is not a CC licence, so FAIL. Fab's CC-BY listings are just Sketchfab mirrors. (2) CGTrader free 'Royalty Free': §21A.3 says to take 'all commercially reasonable measures to prevent the end user from gaining access to the Product' (e.g., encryption), and §21A.2 says in apps the Product must not be downloadable, so FAIL. (3) TurboSquid free: the Royalty Free Licence §II.7(b) requires proprietary formats that 'cannot be opened or imported'; only Unity/Unreal/Lumberyard/Stingray WebGL exports are permitted and 'any other open format' is prohibited, so FAIL for glTF/three.js. (4) Free3D: free models carry per-model licences, mostly 'Personal Use'; the site sits behind a Cloudflare 403, so FAIL/unknown. (5) itch.io: realistic cars there are real-brand replicas (McLaren Artura, Senna, Audi R8 ...) or carry no stated licence, and the rest are PSX/low-poly, so none qualified. (6) Kenney Car Kit, Quaternius cars, Poly Pizza: CC0 but toy/low-poly, rejected on style. (7) BlenderKit: every free CC0 car is a real-brand replica (BMW M4, Ferrari SP3, Bugatti Chiron, Mazda 787B ...), and its non-replica CC0 vehicles need a paid plan, so none qualified. (8) OpenGameArt: mostly low-poly; only the SHC car and the F1 base mesh qualified. (9) Khronos ToyCar: toy, rejected. (10) Stunt Rally / Speed Dreams / TORCS: GPL or Free Art licences, not allowed. Further BlendSwap rejections: 'Supercar Tavaculo (Inspired by Lamborghini)' (CC0, a Lamborghini lookalike), 'Yellow sports car concept' (cut from the author's Corvette C7 model), 'Formula 2 Car' (a Dallara F2 replica), 'Blue and White Muscle Car' (a '65 Mustang), 'PAMERO' (a Camaro), 'Hydra Schmidt Coupe' (a movie car).
